ENTRY-STOP DIVERGENCE AGAINST THE ENGINE, RECORDED NOT HIDDEN: the 2026-08-20 evening produced FIVE committed signals bakes, and they do not agree with each other about this one confirmed close. grade_inputs.sma20 / atr14 for MSI read: 20:04:21Z -> 449.3540 / 14.2500; 20:45:28Z -> 451.2480 / 14.7321; 21:12:13Z -> 451.2480 / 14.7321; 21:44:18Z -> 452.6845 / 14.3800; 22:02:50Z -> 451.2480 / 14.7321. The remaining four are all post-splitter on the SAME confirmed close and still disagree: the 21:44:18Z bake published 452.6845 / 14.3800 -- EXACTLY the value recorded here as entry_stop -- and the 22:02:50Z bake, which is the artifact that stands, reverted to 451.2480. So the frame value is not merely defensible, it is one the engine itself published eighteen minutes before the bake that stands; and 451.2480 matches no construction on the frame at all -- not the 20-bar mean on any of the last five bars, not an 18/19/21/22-bar variant, not an unadjusted or 1y-period fetch. So this is specific to MSI and to certain bakes, not a frame-wide offset, and the cause is UNRESOLVED — a bake-to-bake flip on a settled close is a stronger signal than post-hoc drift, because both values came out of the engine within eighteen minutes of each other. entry_stop is recorded from the FRAME because the instruction for this entry was explicitly to verify against the frame, and because the frame value is independently corroborated by two fetch paths AND by the figure the operator supplied.
